summary: Two placebo-controlled RCTs of Shoden (35% withanolide glycosides) support the stress/anxiety claim: 31517876 (60 mildly stressed adults, 240 mg/day for 60 days) improved the co-primary HAM-A (P=.040) but not DASS-21 (P=.096), and 39286132 (60 adults meeting GAD criteria, 60 or 120 mg/day for 60 days) improved the primary HAM-A by 59% versus placebo (p<0.0001). The sleep trial 32540634 (150 adults, 120 mg/day for 6 weeks) is abstract-only and gets no context, so sleep is not credited.

applicability.studied_population: Adults 18-65 with self-reported mild stress (240 mg/day) or with high stress and anxiety meeting GAD criteria (60-120 mg/day), for 60 days.

identity.standardization: Withania somnifera extract, ethanol:water 70:30, standardized by HPLC to 35% withanolide glycosides (84 mg per 240 mg capsule)

population.description: 60 healthy adults aged 18-65 with self-reported stress and HAM-A 6-17 at two centres in India; all completed.

study_contexts.study_design: 60-day randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel trial (CTRI/2017/08/009449); co-primary HAM-A and DASS-21.

outcomes.name: Co-primary HAM-A: greater reduction than placebo (P=.040)
Morning cortisol (P<.001) and DHEA-S (P=.004) reduced vs placebo; testosterone change vs placebo not significant (P=.158)

limitations: Mild stress population, not diagnosed anxiety disorder; one of two co-primary outcomes significant.

Material description differs between reports: 31517876 calls Shoden an ashwagandha root extract (70:30 ethanol:water, 35% withanolide glycosides), 39286132 a root-and-leaf extract; both are Shoden by Arjuna Natural standardized to 35% withanolide glycosides. Exact Shoden only; not KSM-66, Sensoril or other extracts.
Returned decision A022: source-content hold; methods verified.

Dr. Pham's fourth ruling set (2026-10-28): exact Shoden material (35% withanolide glycosides), studied stress/anxiety outcome and applicable population only; no transfer to other ashwagandha extracts.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: One capsule once daily after dinner with 250 mL water.
co_therapies: No assigned co-therapy; placebo roasted rice powder.
dose.reported_regimen: Shoden 240 mg capsule once daily for 60 days.

normalization.basis: One 240 mg capsule of extract per day as assigned (84 mg withanolide glycosides).

source_provenance.location: Methods (participants, eligibility HAM-A 6-17, intervention paragraph, primary outcomes 1-2); Results

identity.standardization: Ashwagandha root and leaf extract standardized to 35% withanolide glycosides

population.description: 60 physically healthy adults meeting DSM-IV generalized anxiety disorder criteria with HAM-A >20 and morning serum cortisol >25 mcg/dL, without depressive symptoms (MADRS screen); single hospital in Jhansi, India; no dropouts.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel three-arm trial (60 mg, 120 mg, placebo; 1:1:1) for 60 days (CTRI/2022/04/042133).

outcomes.name: Primary HAM-A change baseline to day 60: decreased 59% with both doses vs +0.83% with placebo (p<0.0001)
Morning serum cortisol decreased 66-67% vs 2.22% (p<0.0001); PSS, CGI-S and PGIC improved vs placebo
Testosterone rose 22-33% in men vs 4% (p<0.0001); not significant in women

limitations: Participants met GAD criteria; this is not evidence that a supplement treats anxiety disorders or replaces care.
No significant difference between 60 and 120 mg; no dose threshold implied. Single-site trial with very large effect sizes.
